neighbours.label: the word right after 'under' when 'under' means authority, guidance or grouping (under the supervision of, under one roof), not physical position
fire: The orchestra flourished for a decade under the baton of its young Finnish conductor.
All twelve agencies were brought together under one ministry after the reform.
The project was completed under the guidance of a senior engineer from the city.
Students may use the lab only under the supervision of a qualified instructor.
The company grew rapidly under whose management the profits doubled every year.
The festival is held each spring under the patronage of the regional government.
Several small charities now operate under a single umbrella organisation.
The research was carried out under the auspices of the national science academy.
quiet: The cat spent the whole afternoon hiding under the sofa in the living room.
They found the old letters stored under a loose board in the attic floor.
Water had pooled under the sink because a pipe was slowly leaking.
The children crawled under the fence to fetch the ball from the garden.
She kept a spare key taped under the doormat by the back entrance.
Termites can build their nests under a concrete slab beside the house.
The divers swam under the pier to look at the barnacles on the posts.
Snow had piled up under the bridge after three days of storms.

notes: Card: + pole peaks on ' the'/' one'/' whose' right after 'under' in 'under the direction of', 'under one cover', 'under whose leadership'; output promotes umbrella, auspices, banner, roof. The - pole peaks on physical 'under' (under concrete slabs, underneath their mattress). Near misses use physical 'under'.
